paragraphs: Decision center: The work of a dishwasher is to turn hygiene requirements such as separating dirty from clean dishes and cookware and equipment, the washing and sanitizing process, returning and restocking items, and cleaning the back-of-house areas into a washing chain that is visible in the restaurant and cafeteria back of house, can be picked up by co-workers and can be handed over cleanly at the end of the shift — first collect by category and scrape residue and pre-wash, then wash and sanitize and dry according to the process, then return clean dishes and replenish the pass and cabinets and storage, while cleaning equipment and areas and floors and the dining area, taking out the trash and reporting shortages and breakage and equipment anomalies to the shift supervisor. The focus of judgment is not whether you can scrub dishes, but whether every step of the collection—washing—sanitizing—returning—cleaning—handoff chain is clean, timely and checkable, so that the kitchen and the food runners and the storage and the shift supervisor can all continue their work.

Similar names do not mean the same duties: This page is O*NET-SOC 35-9021.00 Dishwashers. Adjacent positions have different duties — dining room and cafeteria attendants and bartender helpers are responsible for front-of-house table setting and assisting with serving food and drinks and clearing and cleaning, food preparation workers are responsible for prepping and cutting and portioning, restaurant cooks are responsible for preparing dishes and serving, cleaners and building cleaners are responsible for routine cleaning of buildings and public areas, and food service managers are responsible for store operations and staff and costs. The focus of this occupation is washing and sanitizing and returning and trash removal and material handling in the back of house and washing area. Requirements for cleaning and sanitizing food-contact surfaces and for employee health management are governed by the laws of the relevant jurisdiction and the institution's rules, are not inferred from the job title, and no one may change the washing and sanitizing process on their own or promise hygiene results externally.

Inputs that must be checked: the washing and sanitizing process and water temperature and chemical concentration requirements for the shift, the location of dishware washing and sanitizing and storage facilities, the dirty-clean separation and storage standards for dishes and cookware, the status of washing equipment and hot water and drainage and electricity, the use and storage and labeling of detergents and sanitizers, the shortage and breakage and equipment anomaly list, and the shift supervisor's shift instructions and personal hygiene requirements and the pre-work health check performed by the food safety manager. What must not be done: do not skip washing and sanitizing steps or lower water temperature and concentration, do not mix detergents and sanitizers or use them above the stated concentration, do not return unwashed or unsanitized dishes and containers to storage and serving areas, do not store cleaning products together with food and dishes, do not dismantle or repair washing equipment or electrical and drainage facilities on your own, and do not use back-of-house and dining area information or co-workers' personal information for purposes other than service.

The fit judgment should be made by considering whether you can stand and lift for long periods and work under heat and wet floors and noise, whether you can keep motions and records accurate according to the washing and sanitizing sequence, whether you can maintain hygiene and safety standards during meal peaks, whether you can hand off clearly with front and back colleagues, and whether you are clear about your duties and authorization boundaries; it should not be replaced by a self-assessment of having done housework or being able to endure hardship; all of these must be confirmed in supervised actual positions and a trial period.

Core purpose

Make the collection, washing, sanitizing, returning and area cleaning of dishes and cookware from dirty to clean clean, timely and handoffable: dishes usable, washing area tidy, materials replenished by someone, trash removed by someone.

Main objects and basis

The objects are dishes and glassware and pots and cookware, washing and sanitizing and storage facilities and equipment, detergents and sanitizers and cleaning supplies, pass and storage materials, trash and the waste collection area, and dining tables and floors; the basis is the washing and sanitizing process and water temperature and chemical concentration requirements for the shift, dirty-clean separation and storage standards, washing and sanitizing and storage facility requirements, the relevant requirements of the Operation Specifications for Food Safety in Catering Services and the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China, and the shift supervisor's on-site instructions.

Core process

Collect by category and scrape and pre-wash → wash according to the process and apply sanitizing and drying and draining and holding per procedure → check the results and return and replenish → clean equipment and areas and the dining area → remove trash and move materials → log shortages and breakage and equipment anomalies and hand off.

Main outputs

Dishes and cookware washed and sanitized according to the process, storage and holding areas returned to position, serving and storage materials replenished, a clean washing area and floors and dining area, trash removed, and registration and handover records of shortages and breakage and equipment anomalies.

Outputs of adjacent positions: table setting and service and clearing records; cutting and portioning results; dishes that pass the serving standard; cleaning and consumable records; operating statements and scheduling and inspection records.
Responsible party

This occupation bears execution responsibility in the back-of-house washing and cleaning process, and whether the actions are clean, timely and handoffable is the responsibility of the person themselves and the shift leader; requirements for cleaning and sanitizing food-contact surfaces and for employee health management are implemented jointly by the institution and the person themselves.

Responsibilities of adjacent positions: front-of-house service is borne by attendants and helpers; prepping and cutting are borne by food preparation workers; dish preparation and serving are borne by the kitchen; building and public area cleaning is borne by cleaners; operating and compliance responsibility is borne by managers.

Collaborate with the kitchen and the pass, food runners and front of house, storage and purchasing, cleaning and equipment maintenance, and the shift supervisor, adjusting priorities according to shift instructions and the meal peak rhythm; report anomalies and unauthorized matters immediately.

Collaboration of adjacent positions: attendants and helpers connect with front of house and the kitchen; food preparation connects with the kitchen and storage; the kitchen connects with the pass; cleaners connect with each area and property management; managers connect with each position and with suppliers.

Chapter 14 of the 2018 Operation Specifications for Food Safety in Catering Services is the one covering health and training and hygiene, not Chapters 11 and 12. 14.1.1 covers persons in contact with ready-to-eat food, including the corresponding processing, food running and dishware washing and sanitizing, and new or temporary personnel, who must first obtain a health certificate and be examined annually; 14.1.2 requires the food safety manager to check health before each day's shift, report fever and diarrhea and the like, suspend direct ready-to-eat work, identify the cause, and return to work only after the related disease is cured, with return to work not authorized by the person themselves or by AI. 14.2 requires passing training and assessment before taking up a post, with enterprises assessed annually and specific providers every six months. The 2021 text of the Food Safety Law, Articles 33(5), 45, 56, 58 and 126(5)(6), respectively support washing and sanitizing dishware before use, health certificates for ready-to-eat food handlers, washing and sanitizing by catering units or compliant outsourced centralized sanitizing, batch testing and packaging by centralized sanitizing units, and penalties. The third amendment decision of 2025 has taken effect (2025-12-01) and changes only Articles 41, 81, 82, 124 and 132, without changing these related articles; the original 2015 link is not treated as the 2025 full text. Article 23 of the 2019 implementing regulations concerns food irradiation, and the old Article 23 wording on job reassignment is no longer cited as a current article number; Articles 26 and 27 of the 2019 regulations concern retention of outsourcing certificates and centralized sanitizing records, and Article 28 concerns the system for canteens serving meals centrally, so the main responsibility cannot all be shifted to an individual dishwasher.
